data.title: Target sets its fall sales event for the same days as Amazon's
data.description:
Target Corporation (TGT) announced on Tuesday that its fall Target Circle Deal Days event will run October 6–7 in a direct challenge to Amazon's (AMZN) Prime Big Deal Days shopping event. The retailer will offer Target Circle members up to 40% off thousands of products. The promotion spans fall apparel, home décor, kitchen tools, beauty, toys, technology, and early holiday merchandise. As a perk, Target Circle 360 members can begin shopping select offers on October 5.

The Minneapolis-based company's strategy is focused on budget-conscious seasonal shopping, such as replacing summer clothing, refreshing homes for fall, and starting holiday gift purchases early. Promoted offers include 40% off select family apparel and outdoor holiday décor, 30% off selected Threshold furniture and Hearth & Hand with Magnolia products, discounts on select Dyson vacuums, and savings of up to 40% on toys, laptops, and other tech. Target (TGT) also aims to use the event to recruit and deepen loyalty membership.

The annual fall sales event evolved from Target Circle Week, a longer loyalty-sale format. In fall 2025, Target held a seven-day Circle Week from October 5–11, featuring discounts of up to 50% and daily deals.

Shares of Target (TGT) were down 2.0% in Tuesday afternoon trading.

data.title: Scholar Rock downgraded at Barclays despite FDA approval of SMA therapy
data.description:
Scholar Rock (SRRK) shares continued to tumble on Tuesday as Barclays downgraded the Massachusetts-area biotech despite last week’s FDA approval of its lead asset, Isembyld, for spinal muscular atrophy, a rare neuromuscular disorder.

Despite a 7% YTD gain, Scholar Rock (SRRK) has lost more than 14% since Friday, when the company became a commercial-stage biotech following the FDA nod for Isembyld as a late-line option for those aged two years and older with SMA.  

However, Barclays analyst Etzer Darout cut his rating on SRRK to Equal Weight from Overweight, citing a more balanced risk-reward setup post-approval and indicating a cautious tone on the company’s non-SMA pipeline.

“While we continue to view these programs as important sources of long-term optionality, our valuation today remains driven primarily by the SMA opportunity. We believe additional clinical validation will likely be required before we can ascribe meaningful incremental value to the broader pipeline beyond SMA,” Darout wrote.

The analyst argued that future upside to his above-consensus estimates will increasingly depend on a commercial execution that could surpass his expectations and the company’s pipeline expansion opportunities beyond SMA.

However, Darout raised his price target on Scholar Rock (SRRK) to $58 from $55 per share, noting that the pricing the management announced for Isembyld on Monday slightly exceeded his prior estimates.

data.title: Transocean jumps after securing $80M ultra-deepwater rig contract
data.description:
Transocean (RIG) rises 8.6% in Tuesday's trading after saying its Deepwater Conqueror ultra-deepwater drillship was awarded a two-well contract for work in Equatorial Guinea by an undisclosed operator.

The company said the estimated 170-day campaign is expected to begin in 2027 in direct continuation of the rig's current contract in the U.S. Gulf and contribute ~$80M in backlog, excluding additional services and compensation for mobilization and demobilization.

Transocean (RIG) owns or has partial ownership interests in and operates a fleet of 27 mobile offshore drilling units, consisting of 20 ultra-deepwater floaters and seven harsh environment floaters.

The company said in August that Africa would drive demand for new deepwater contracts, with the gain expected to offset a decline in U.S. Gulf-based contracts.

data.title: Trump out-traded all members of Congress combined - report
data.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump and his wealth managers executed nearly 28.7K security transactions in the 17 months following his second inauguration—outpacing all members of Congress combined—even as he pushes legislation banning lawmakers from buying stocks, according to a media report Tuesday.

During that same period, Capitol Hill lawmakers collectively reported about 22.2K similar transactions, Bloomberg reported, citing security transaction disclosure forms.

The contrast marks a notable shift from his first term, when Trump's financial disclosures contained mostly illiquid real estate holdings and other privately held ventures. His portfolio now spans thousands of holdings in stocks (SPY) (DIA) (QQQ), bonds (TLT) (SHY) and cryptocurrencies (IBIT) (ETHA).

The stock-purchasing ban passed by House Republicans in July exclusively restricts members of Congress, their spouses and dependent children. The legislation leaves the presidency untouched—even though the commander-in-chief has singularly wide-ranging access to U.S. intelligence and the power to influence entire sectors with an executive order or social media post.

Backing the proposed House measure, Trump had stated in his recent State of the Union address that it must be enacted "without delay" so that members of Congress "cannot corruptly profit from using insider information." He remains the only U.S. president this century to disclose active trading of individual stocks, continuing transactions that would be prohibited for lawmakers under the very legislation he champions.

In June alone, Trump made more than 1K securities trades, including significant purchases of Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B), Visa (V), Mastercard (MA), Palantir (PLTR) and Cintas (CTAS), financial disclosure published by the U.S. Office of Government Ethics. The largest transaction was a June 22 sale of between $5M and $25M of shares in the Vanguard Dividend Appreciation Index Fund ETF (VIG).

data.title: RTX CEO sees defense, aerospace demand supporting cash-flow growth
data.description:
RTX (RTX) Chairman and Chief Executive Chris Calio on Tuesday said strong demand for air travel and rising global defense spending should support the aerospace and defense company’s growth for years, while increased factory automation and long-term military contracts help address production constraints.

Speaking with Morgan Stanley analyst Christine Liwag at the firm’s 14th Annual Laguna Conference, Calio said airlines continue to need newer, more fuel-efficient aircraft. He also pointed to heightened geopolitical threats that are prompting countries to increase defense spending and strengthen their domestic security capabilities.

For investors, Calio’s comments highlighted the breadth of RTX’s (RTX) exposure to two durable markets. Its commercial aerospace businesses stand to benefit from rising aircraft production and aftermarket demand, while Raytheon is positioned for spending on missiles, radar systems and layered air defense. The principal challenge is execution, including expanding capacity and ensuring that suppliers can keep pace.

Defense backlog leaves room for additional awards

RTX (RTX) has a backlog of about $289 billion, according to Calio. That figure does not include five framework agreements covering major munitions programs or a recently awarded seven-year, $23 billion Tomahawk contract.

Volumes under the five agreements could rise by two to four times, Calio said. Their multiyear structure gives RTX (RTX) and its suppliers greater confidence to invest in equipment, facilities and employees.

That visibility is particularly important because about half of the company’s supply chain consists of small and midsize businesses. Some suppliers have been reluctant or unable to add capacity without firm orders extending beyond the government’s traditional annual procurement cycle.

Raytheon spans multiple layers of missile defense

Calio said Raytheon operates “right at the heart” of integrated air and missile defense. Sensors and effectors account for about 70% of the unit’s sales.

Its portfolio includes the Coyote counter-drone system, NASAMS, Patriot, the LTAMDS radar, SPY-6 naval radar and the Standard Missile family. Coyote has recorded more than 600 drone defeats in operational settings, Calio said. Raytheon also is developing a reusable, non-kinetic version that employs high-powered microwaves against drone swarms.

RTX (RTX) expects demand for sophisticated weapons to remain strong even as the Pentagon seeks cheaper systems that can be manufactured in larger numbers. Calio described the market as an “and, not an or,” with lower-cost weapons complementing high-end missiles and sensors rather than replacing them.

Raytheon also is working on a modular weapons approach that combines existing components, including seekers, actuators and power systems. The goal is to shorten development cycles and respond more quickly to changing military needs.

International demand supports further expansion

About 48% of Raytheon’s backlog is international, up four percentage points from a year earlier. Calio said the company’s installed base and international production partnerships should help it compete as governments seek greater domestic involvement in weapons manufacturing.

He cited Patriot and NASAMS deployments across Europe and the Middle East, along with partnerships involving Kongsberg and MBDA. RTX also recently announced a Coyote co-production agreement with the United Arab Emirates.

The company has about 20,000 employees in Europe and is evaluating additional European suppliers for AMRAAM and Stinger. Calio said these arrangements can expand the supply base while strengthening relationships with foreign customers.

Commercial aftermarket outlook remains strong

On the commercial side, Calio said Boeing and Airbus both want to increase production. RTX expects to deliver a record number of geared turbofan engines this year and is investing to remain aligned with the aircraft manufacturers’ planned rate increases.

Although higher jet-fuel prices have pressured airlines, RTX has not seen a meaningful change in customer purchasing behavior, he said.

Calio pointed to a large pool of future maintenance work across the company’s installed engine base. About 15% of V2500 engines have not undergone their first shop visit and roughly half have not reached their second. At Pratt & Whitney Canada, about 60% of the installed base has yet to receive its first overhaul.

GTF maintenance output rose 40% from a year earlier in the second quarter, helping reduce aircraft-on-ground levels by 25% since the end of 2025. RTX has added seven GTF maintenance shops over the past three years, with newer locations reducing turnaround times for heavy shop visits by nearly 20%.

Cash conversion and margins offer upside

RTX continues to target a medium-term operating margin of 19% to 20% at Collins Aerospace. Calio identified commercial aftermarket growth, increased original-equipment production and structural cost reductions as the main drivers.

The company expects 2026 free cash flow of about $8.6 billion at the midpoint of its forecast. Calio declined to give a specific estimate for 2027, but said RTX’s longer-term fundamentals should support free cash flow equal to roughly 90% to 100% of adjusted net income.

RTX’s capital priorities remain investment in production capacity, debt reduction and dividends. Calio said the company expects debt to return to levels seen before its accelerated share-repurchase program by year-end. He also described the dividend as “sacrosanct,” signaling that shareholder payouts will remain a central part of the company’s capital-allocation strategy.

data.title: GE Vernova inches higher after big drop; analyst says company still 'wired to win'
data.description:
GE Vernova (GEV) gains 0.4% in Tuesday's trading, a day after the stock's 8.5% swoon as GLJ Research downgraded shares to Sell and investors feared that a backlash against AI spending could expose the company to canceled orders.

Bernstein analyst Sunaina Ocalan backed the company on Tuesday, saying GE Vernova (GEV) is still "wired to win" and that the stock is not all about data centers.

"While data center orders were $5 billion in [H1 2026], or about 38% of electrification orders, the remaining 62% was utility-driven," Ocalan said in a note. "Utility spend should continue to grow, supported by grid reliability and resilience investments. A slowdown in data center demand may alleviate generation bottlenecks but would do little to address existing grid constraints."

Bernstein rates GE Vernova (GEV) as a Buy with a $1,298 price target, and nearly 80% of Wall Street analysts covering the company consider the stock a Buy, according to FactSet.

Separately, GE Vernova (GEV) announced an agreement with Eurus Energy Holdings to supply seven 4.2 MW, 117-meter wind turbines for the 29.4 MW Eurus Hiyamizutouge wind farm in Japan, part of its accelerating work in Japan's expanding wind energy market.

GE Vernova (GEV) said its technology powers about half of Japan's installed heavy-duty gas turbine capacity and a quarter of the country's onshore wind capacity.

data.title: Weekly ETFs: Eight of 11 sectors record outflows; the financial sector leads inflows
data.description:

data.title: Realty Income stock nears its 52-week low: Is selloff a buying chance?
data.description:
Realty Income (O) stock has been under pressure for a week, but the selloff may say more about interest rates than the REIT’s underlying business.

The shares were recently trading around $58.93 on Tuesday, down 2.26% over the past week and close to the 52-week low of $55.86. 

On a YTD basis, Realty Income has gained just 4.52%, lagging the 11.31% advance in the S&P 500 (SP500).

The short-term chart remains firmly bearish. The stock has fallen from roughly $61.60 at the start of the week to $58.87, forming lower highs and lower lows.

 A break below $59 added to the selling pressure, while higher volume during several declines suggests active selling. RSI at 31.70 is approaching oversold territory, while the MACD at -0.1858 remains below its signal line, keeping momentum bearish.

A sustained move back above $59 would be an early sign of stabilization.

Still, the fundamental picture is more resilient. Seeking Alpha analyst Danil Sereda remains bullish, pointing to Realty Income’s 98.8% portfolio occupancy, growing capital-light operations, and institutional partnerships.

He sees more than 25% upside over the next 12–16 months, with a $74.85 valuation target and a Buy rating.

Recent moves support that view. Realty Income and KKR & Co. (KKR) launched a European joint venture, with KKR-advised investors committing €528M for roughly 49% of the venture.

Moreover, the company also raised its monthly dividend to $0.2715 per share, its 136th increase.

Ratings remain mixed: SA Analysts: Buy (3.88), Wall Street: Buy (3.50), while Quant: Hold (2.92).

For now, the chart says "caution," but the fundamentals suggest the selloff may be creating an increasingly interesting setup if interest rate pressure eases.

data.title: Wall Street slides as yields remain in focus ahead of the FOMC rate decision
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages declined Tuesday as Treasury yields remained the focal point and investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision later this week.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last -0.9%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last -0.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last -0.7%.

From a sector-by-sector vantage point, 10 of the 11 segments were in the red and were led lower by consumer discretionary. At the other end of the spectrum, energy was the strongest performer as oil (CL1:COM) advanced. 

The bond-market selloff adds pressure ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision Wednesday, with investors expecting officials to raise short-term borrowing costs for the first time since July 2023.

The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) inched down 1 basis point to 4.66%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield (US10Y) ticked higher by 1 basis point to 5.00%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) pushed up 2 basis points to 5.37%. 

“The Federal Reserve has little choice but to hike rates on Wednesday, especially since the bond market has been signaling for weeks that higher rates are warranted, given warm inflation data, strong earnings and a sturdy labor market. The stock market would be disappointed if the Fed didn't hike rates on Wednesday,” Carol Schleif of BMO Wealth Management stated.

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of QUALCOMM (QCOM) +4.1%, while shares of Coinbase (COIN) fell -5.9%

data.title: Installed Building Products wins Buy rating at Stifel on housing recovery, M&A
data.description:
Stifel on Tuesday initiated coverage of Installed Building Products (IBP) with a Buy rating, citing the insulation installer’s resilient revenue, strong margins and acquisition opportunities.

Installed Building Products operates more than 250 U.S. branches and is the country’s second-largest residential insulation installer behind QXO (QXO). New residential construction accounts for 73% of installed revenue, followed by commercial construction at 20% and residential repair and remodeling at 7%.

For investors, Stifel’s thesis hinges on IBP weathering the housing downturn until residential construction improves. The firm also sees acquisitions, share repurchases and dividends supporting returns while investors wait. IBP shares had fallen 28% this year through Sept. 11, compared with an 11.9% gain for the S&P 500.

The company’s same-branch revenue increased 0.8% from 2022 through the 12 months ended in the second quarter of 2026, according to Stifel. That compares with a 4% decline in U.S. housing completions and a 6.6% drop in organic revenue among building-products distributors. IBP’s EBITDA margin expanded by 58 basis points to 17%, about 550 basis points above its peer group.

Stifel forecasts revenue rising from $3.01 billion in 2026 to $3.15 billion in 2027 and $3.32 billion in 2028. Adjusted earnings are projected to increase from $10.69 a share in 2026 to $11.79 in 2027 and $13.01 in 2028, representing a two-year compound annual growth rate of 10.3%.

Acquisitions remain another part of the bullish case. IBP has completed more than 100 purchases since its 2014 initial public offering, adding over $1.2 billion in annual revenue. Stifel estimated that M&A could add nearly 11 percentage points to shareholder returns during the next two and a half years if IBP deploys its available cash flow and balance-sheet capacity.

Risks include elevated interest rates, weaker housing demand, labor constraints, customer concentration and inflation in insulation products. Stifel also warned that aggressive behavior from IBP’s largest competitor and a shift away from higher-priced spray-foam insulation could weigh on its outlook.

Stifel's price target of $240 represents about 17% upside from IBP’s Sept. 11 closing price of $204.28. Analyst W. Andrew Carter based the valuation on slightly more than 13 times estimated 2027 EBITDA, assuming the stock regains a larger premium over building-products distribution peers.
